title: run/event
description: One run event, reported by the runner as the actor works. The first event is init; a run that ends on its own ends with exactly one result.

event.title: Run event
event.description: Every event carries the run id, a seq that starts at 0 and increases by one, and a type.

hostEvent.title: Run event as troupe passes it on
hostEvent.description: A run event, or the oversized event troupe writes in place of one larger than the maximum event size. As troupe records it, an init may lack effects: one recorded before runners said how they apply effects.

init.title: init
init.description: Always seq 0: what the actor runs with.

effects.description: How the runner applies the actor's declared effects. checked: it checks each change its engine asks for against them before carrying it out. translated: it translates them into its engine's own rules. A runner always sends it (see event); it's absent only from an init troupe recorded before runners said how they apply effects.

engine.description: The engine the runner drives, where there is one.

version.description: The engine's version. Absent: the runner doesn't know it.

model.description: The model the engine runs. Absent: it has none, or the runner doesn't know it.

tools.description: The tools available to the actor.

tool_result.title: tool_result
tool_result.description: The result of an earlier tool_call with the same callId. The full output belongs in the transcript.

retry.title: retry
retry.description: The engine is retrying, for example an API call.

maxAttempts.description: How many attempts the engine will make in all. Absent: the engine doesn't say.

message.description: The engine's own words about the retry. Absent: it gave none.

context.title: context
context.description: Content of the run's conversation was compacted or dropped, by the engine or the runner, and the run carries on. Sent when it happens. A loss that ends the run is reported by the result instead.

kind.description: What happened. compacted: earlier content was replaced by a summary of it. truncated: earlier content was dropped outright. other: a loss neither names; the message says what was lost.

by.description: Who reduced the conversation. engine: the engine, on its own. runner: the runner, in the conversation it holds and sends to its engine.

tokensBefore.description: Tokens the conversation held before the loss, as the engine or runner reports them. Absent: not known.

tokensAfter.description: Tokens the conversation held after the loss, as the engine or runner reports them. Absent: not known.

messagesBefore.description: Messages the conversation held before the loss. Absent: not known.

messagesAfter.description: Messages the conversation held after the loss. Absent: not known.

log.title: log
log.description: A runner diagnostic worth keeping with the run.

served_model.title: served_model
served_model.description: A model other than the one init named answered part of the run. Sent the first time each such model answers, before any event reporting that answer; never for init's model, and never twice for one model.

model.description: The model that answered, as the engine or service named it.

result.title: result
result.description: What the runner saw at the end. status is error whenever the engine reported an error, whatever else it reported alongside it. An error result says why in reason; an ok result has none. It carries a reported cost or an estimate, never both.

reason.description: Why the run failed. Present exactly when status is error. Absent: status is ok.

turns.description: How many turns the engine took. Absent: the engine doesn't count them.

durationMs.description: How long the run took, by the engine's clock. Absent: the engine doesn't report it.

usage.description: Token counts, where the engine reports them. inputTokens, cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens add up to the run's whole input.

inputTokens.description: Input tokens not counted in cacheReadTokens or cacheWriteTokens. A runner subtracts whatever its engine's input count includes of the cache's reads and writes; input it can't separate into a cache counter stays in inputTokens. Absent: the engine doesn't report them.

outputTokens.description: Output tokens the engine used. Absent: the engine doesn't report them.

cacheReadTokens.description: Input tokens read from the engine's prompt cache. Absent: the runner couldn't report them, and never estimates them.

cacheWriteTokens.description: Input tokens written to the engine's prompt cache. Absent: the runner couldn't report them, and never estimates them.

costUsd.description: What the run cost in US dollars, as the engine or its service reported it; never worked out by the runner. Absent: nothing reported a cost.

estimatedCostUsd.description: An estimate, not a reported cost: the run's usage at the price troupe gave in run/start's runtime.price, in US dollars. Sent only when nothing reported a cost and run/start carried a price. Absent: no price, or the usage has a kind of token the price has no rate for, or a rate for a counter that wasn't reported.

failureReason.title: Failure reason
failureReason.description: Why a run failed, from a closed list troupe can act on the same way for every runner. A failure the list has no entry for is other, and the result's message says what happened; a runner can't add reasons of its own. The four a retry can also name mean the same on both, so a run whose retries ran out ends with its last retry's reason. authentication: the engine or service refused the credential. quota: the account is out of quota, credit or billing. rate-limit: rate limited past what the runner will wait or retry. network: the engine couldn't be reached. server: the engine or service kept failing on its side. configuration: the endpoint or model can't serve the run (nothing there, a redirect, no such model). context-length: the conversation outgrew the model's context. output-limit: an answer was cut at the output limit and the runner ended the run for it. refused: the model refused, or the service's content filter stopped it. turn-limit: the runner's or engine's turn limit was reached. budget: the runner's or engine's token or cost budget was spent. cancelled: the run was cancelled and the runner still sent a result. engine: the engine failed in a way of its own, or sent what the runner can't act on. runner: the runner itself failed unexpectedly. other: none of these.

oversized.title: oversized
oversized.description: Written by troupe, never by a runner: stands in for an event larger than the maximum event size. The original is in the artifact store under ref, less any estimatedCostUsd troupe gave the runner no price for.
